ai.description: *Gegeneophis danieli* reaches 25 cm. It is dark violet-grey with a pale snout and vent. Distinctive features include a blunt, rounded head and 115–125 primary annuli.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Gegeneophis danieli* is best distinguished by its lack of secondary annuli, possessing only primary rings that do not encircle the body, unlike most other Indian caecilians.
ai.habitat: Daniel's Caecilian inhabits moist, shaded soil within tropical evergreen forests and plantations in the Western Ghats, typically at elevations between 600 and 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: Daniel's Caecilian is primarily nocturnal, emerging from its subterranean burrows at night to forage for earthworms and other small soil invertebrates.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Gegeneophis danieli* is oviparous, laying clutches of 10–20 eggs in underground burrows. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, with females providing maternal care.
ai.distributionRemarks: Daniel's Caecilian is endemic to the northern Western Ghats in Maharashtra, India, where it is found at elevations between 600 and 1,200 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Gegeneophis danieli* consists of a series of low-pitched, pulsed notes emitted by individuals residing in moist, subterranean soil habitats.
